reasoning: Products have very different attributes: a phone has storage and RAM while a shirt has size and colour. A document model stores each product with its own nested fields, reviews and images, and the schema can change without migrations.
A cart is read and written by session or user ID on every click and needs very low latency. Key-value lookups in memory are ideal, and built-in expiry removes abandoned sessions.

Orders and click events are append-only, arrive in huge volumes, and are queried by customer and time range. Partitioning by customer and clustering by time gives fast writes and efficient range reads at scale.
Suggestions like 'customers who bought this also bought' are multi-hop relationships between users, products and categories. A graph database traverses these links quickly without expensive joins.
